mainTopic: How far the mother's שחיטה reaches for her עובר: the boundary of a fetus, a limb that came out, the offspring and milk of such an animal, and the פסוק that permits the fetus
overview: The גמרא first tries to prove something from the משנה's closing כלל, but pushes the proof off: the extra words teach that a קלוט still inside a cow is permitted, even for רבי שמעון. רב חנניא then asks whether the עזרה counts as the boundary for a fetus of קדשים whose leg came out. אביי answers that a fetus's boundary is always its mother. אילפא asks about a leg that came out between the two סימנים, and רבא uses a קל וחומר to rule that the leg is טהור from נבלה. רבי ירמיה asks about the offspring of such a fetus. After several reframings, the גמרא's real question is whether that animal's milk may be drunk, and it ends in תיקו. Finally, the גמרא looks for the פסוק that permits pieces cut from a fetus. It drops 'בהמה בבהמה' because of the laws of תמורה and uses 'וכל בהמה', limited by 'אותה'. It then raises a challenge from רבי יוחנן's ruling about a dove-shaped fetus, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to learn from the משנה's general principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's כלל and asks what the extra words 'שאינה גופה מותר' come to add, suggesting they include the case under discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: something that is the animal's body is forbidden, and something that is not its body is permitted. What does 'not its body' come to include? Doesn't it come to include a case like this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the closing כלל of the משנה and tries to use its extra words as a proof for the case it was just discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already taught the laws of the fetus before stating the כלל, so the words 'שאינה גופה מותר' seem extra. The גמרא suggests these extra words must come to permit the case under discussion, where the fetus had mostly come out and part was still inside.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule (a summary that often comes to add a new case)
Her body; parts of the mother animal herself
To include; to add another case
Like this kind of case

phrases.english: This is the principle: something that is its body is forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'Its body' means a part of the mother animal herself that was cut off before the שחיטה.

phrases.english: and something that is not its body is permitted.
phrases.notes: 'Not its body' means the fetus inside her.

phrases.english: 'That is not its body' — what does it come to include?
Is it not to include a case like this?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין גּוּפָהּ לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לָאו לְאֵתוֹיֵי כְּהַאי גַּוְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion by bringing a proof from the משנה's closing כלל.
steps.raayaObject: That the part of the fetus still inside the womb is permitted in the case under discussion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra words 'ושאינה גופה מותר' in the משנה's כלל.

steps.title: The extra words include a קלוט inside a cow
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the כלל comes to include a fetus with uncloven hooves found inside a cow, which is permitted even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it comes to include a קלוט inside a cow's womb, according to רבי שמעון. Even though רבי שמעון said a קלוט born from a cow is forbidden, that is only when it came out into the world; but while it is inside its mother, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by finding a different case that the extra words of the כלל come to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון forbids a קלוט (a calf without split hooves) once it is born. The כלל teaches that if it is still inside its mother at her שחיטה, it is permitted as part of her. So the extra words are needed for this, and they prove nothing about our case.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with uncloven (non-split) hooves
Inside the womb of a cow
According to the opinion of
The open air of the world; meaning it was born
Permitted

phrases.english: No, it comes to include a קלוט inside the womb of a cow,
and according to רבי שמעון,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: for even though רבי שמעון said:
a קלוט born from a cow is forbidden —

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּיָצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: that applies only where it came out into the air of the world,
but inside its mother's womb, it is permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: The כלל 'שאינה גופה מותר' teaches that a קלוט still inside its mother at her שחיטה is permitted, even for רבי שמעון.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by giving the extra words a different purpose.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the כלל, not the case itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra words are needed for another case (קלוט inside a cow according to רבי שמעון), so they do not have to refer to our case.

steps.title: A fetus of קדשים sticks its leg out inside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא asks whether the עזרה counts as the fetus's boundary, so its leg that came out is not forbidden, or whether a fetus's boundary is only its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא asked: if a fetus put out its leg inside the עזרה, what is the law? Since the עזרה is the boundary for קדשים, is it also the boundary for this leg? Or perhaps for this it is not a boundary, because the boundary of a fetus is its mother?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: רב חנניא asks what happens when a fetus of a קרבן sticks its leg out of its mother while inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A limb that leaves its boundary becomes forbidden. For קדשי קדשים, the עזרה is their boundary, so maybe the leg never really 'left'. Or maybe for a fetus, the only boundary that matters is its mother, so the leg is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Since; because it is so in one area, it should be so in another
A boundary or partition
Or perhaps (the other side of a question)

phrases.english: רב חנניא asked:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹצִיא עוּבָּר אֶת יָדוֹ בָּעֲזָרָה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If a fetus put out its leg in the עזרה, what is the law?
phrases.notes: This is a fetus of קדשי קדשים, which may only be eaten inside the עזרה.

phrases.english: Since it is a boundary for קדשים —
it is also a boundary for this,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לְגַבֵּי דְּהַאי לָאו מְחִיצָה הִיא,
phrases.english: or perhaps for this it is not a boundary,
because the boundary of a fetus is its mother?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, building on the idea that a limb leaving its boundary becomes forbidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the עזרה counts as a boundary for a fetus of קדשים, so that a leg that came out of the mother inside the עזרה stays permitted.

steps.title: אביי: the boundary of a fetus is its mother
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רב חנניא does not ask the same about קדשים קלים in ירושלים, because there it is obvious the boundary of a fetus is its mother; the same is true in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why don't you ask the same about קדשים קלים in ירושלים? Why don't you ask about them? Because the boundary of a fetus is its mother. Here too, the boundary of a fetus is its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב חנניא by comparing to a case he clearly was not unsure about: קדשים קלים, whose boundary is ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one thinks a fetus of קדשים קלים whose leg came out stays permitted just because it was inside ירושלים. The reason must be that a fetus's boundary is its mother. That same reason applies to קדשי קדשים in the עזרה, so the leg is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, eaten anywhere in ירושלים
What is the reason?
You are not asking (because it is clear to you)
Here too

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
Then ask the same about קדשים קלים in ירושלים!
phrases.notes: קדשים קלים may be eaten anywhere in ירושלים, so the city is their boundary, just like the עזרה is for קדשי קדשים.

phrases.english: With קדשים קלים in ירושלים, what is the reason
that you don't ask?
Because the boundary of a fetus is its mother;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי מְחִיצַת עוּבָּר אִמּוֹ הִוא.
phrases.english: here too, the boundary of a fetus is its mother.

steps.whatToRemember: For a fetus, the only boundary that counts is its mother. If its leg came out of her, even inside the עזרה or ירושלים, that leg is treated as having left its boundary.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear rule: the place-limits of קדשים do not change the fetus's own boundary, which is always its mother.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְתִבְּעֵי לָךְ קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנניא's question in step 3 by comparing to a case he was not unsure about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The boundary of a fetus is its mother, so the עזרה does not help; the leg that came out is forbidden, just as with קדשים קלים in ירושלים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מחיצת עובר אמו היא — the boundary of a fetus is its mother, for קדשי קדשים just as for קדשים קלים.

steps.title: A leg that came out between the first and second cut
steps.stepSummary: אילפא asks: if the fetus stuck out its leg after the first סימן was cut but before the second, do the two cuts combine to keep that leg from being טמא as נבלה?
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא asked: if a fetus put its leg out between the cutting of one סימן and the other, what is the law? Does the first סימן join with the second to make the leg טהור from the טומאה of נבלה, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: אילפא asks a new question. A fetus stuck its leg out of the mother in the middle of the שחיטה, and he wants to know if that leg is saved from the טומאה of נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that once the leg is outside, the שחיטה cannot make it permitted to eat, but it does save it from being טמא as נבלה. Here the leg was still inside during the first cut and outside during the second cut. Can two cuts that happened under different conditions add up to one full שחיטה for this leg?

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two pipes (windpipe and food pipe) that must be cut in שחיטה
Combines, joins together
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; it is forbidden and makes things טמא
To make it טהור (pure)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is NOT whether the leg may be eaten. It cannot be, because it was outside during the second cut. The only question is whether it is saved from the טומאה of נבלה.

phrases.english: Ilfa asked:
If a fetus put out its leg
between one siman and the other, what is the law?
phrases.notes: After the first pipe was cut but before the second one was cut.

phrases.aramaic: מִי מִצְטָרֵף סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: Does the first siman join with the second siman
to make it pure from the impurity of a carcass, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question built on the earlier rule that a leg that came out is forbidden to eat but saved from נבלה טומאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the cutting of the first סימן (leg inside) and the second סימן (leg outside) combine to save the leg from נבלה טומאה.

steps.title: רבא proves it with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a קל וחומר: if the two cuts combine for the strict matter of permitting the fetus to be eaten, surely they combine for the lighter matter of keeping the leg טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is a קל וחומר. If the first סימן joined with the second to permit the fetus to be eaten, will it not help to make the leg טהור from the טומאה of נבלה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אילפא's question with a קל וחומר: yes, the two cuts combine and the leg is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the fetus stayed inside, and the first and second cuts together permit it to be eaten. Permitting food is a bigger thing than just saving from טומאה. So if the cuts combine for the bigger thing, they surely combine to save the leg from טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a rule applies in the stricter case, it surely applies in the lighter case
Helped, was effective
To permit it for eating

steps.whatToRemember: A leg that came out between the two סימנים is טהור from נבלה, because the two cuts combine.

phrases.english: Rava said: it is an a fortiori argument,

phrases.aramaic: אִם הוֹעִיל לוֹ סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: if the first siman helped together with the second siman
to permit it for eating,
phrases.notes: He means the rest of the fetus, which stayed inside the mother the whole time.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יוֹעִיל לוֹ לְטַהוֹרֵיהּ מִידֵי נְבֵלָה?
phrases.english: will it not help it to make it pure from the impurity of a carcass?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אילפא's question directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the cuts combine and the leg is טהור, by a קל וחומר from permitting the fetus to be eaten.

steps.title: Must we worry about the offspring?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the איסור on a fetus whose leg came out passes on to its offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: what is the law about worrying over its offspring?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question: if this fetus, with its forbidden leg, lives and has babies, do we have to worry that the babies are affected by that איסור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fetus's leg became forbidden when it came out. The question is whether that איסור carries over into the next generation. The גמרא will next try to work out what case he means.

keyTerms.meaning: To worry, to be concerned about an איסור
Its offspring

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
what is the law, must we be concerned about its offspring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about the same kind of fetus, now about its offspring.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the איסור of the leg that came out passes on to the fetus's offspring.

steps.title: Which case does רבי ירמיה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי ירמיה means. If the animal mated with a normal animal, why ask about this animal in particular?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it mated with a normal, fully kosher animal, why ask specifically about this one, which has an איסור from going out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defining the case of רבי ירמיה's question. It tries one option and pushes it away, setting up a better explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the question were about this animal mating with a normal animal, it would be a general question about any forbidden animal mating with a permitted one. That is not special to an animal with an איסור of going out, so רבי ירמיה would not need to ask it here. This tells us his question must be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (a suggestion that is about to be pushed away)
A normal, fully kosher animal
Why specifically this? Why single this out?
The איסור that comes from a limb going out of its boundary

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it mated with a normal animal,
why ask specifically about this one
which has in it the prohibition of going out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case behind רבי ירמיה's question and rejects the first possible reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case רבי ירמיה's question is about, since the case of mating with a normal animal would not be special to this fetus.

steps.title: Any בן פקועה that mates with a normal animal has this problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its question from step 8 with רב משרשיא's rule: according to the view that the father's status counts, a בן פקועה that mates with a normal animal produces offspring that can never be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even an ordinary בן פקועה has this problem. רב משרשיא said: according to the view that we take the father into account, if a בן פקועה mates with a regular animal, the offspring has no way to become permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is proving its point from step 8. If רבי ירמיה meant mating with a normal animal, the offspring would be a problem for any בן פקועה, so why single out this one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother is a normal animal, so the offspring needs שחיטה. The father is a בן פקועה, whose kind does not need שחיטה, so שחיטה does not work for it. Caught between both, the offspring can never be permitted, so that case cannot be what רבי ירמיה is asking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus found alive inside a slaughtered mother; the mother's שחיטה permits it
We take the father's status into account, not only the mother's
A full-fledged, normal animal
It has no fix; there is no way to make it permitted

phrases.english: Even an ordinary בן פקועה would also have this problem,
as רב משרשיא said:
According to the one who says we take the father's seed into account,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן פְּקוּעָה הַבָּא עַל בְּהֵמָה מְעַלַּיְיתָא –
phrases.english: a בן פקועה that mated with a regular, full-fledged animal:
the offspring has no way to become permitted.
phrases.notes: The mother's side says it needs שחיטה, and the father's side says שחיטה doesn't work for it, so nothing helps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ בֶּן פְּקוּעָה דְּעָלְמָא נָמֵי, דְּאָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind step 8's question
steps.raayaObject: That mating with a normal animal cannot be רבי ירמיה's case
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב משרשיא's rule that the offspring of a בן פקועה and a normal animal has no fix

steps.title: The case is a fetus that mated with another בן פקועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ירמיה is asking about a fetus that mated with another בן פקועה like itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed for a case where it mated with a בן פקועה like itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 8's question by narrowing the case: both parents are בני פקועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both parents are בני פקועה, the offspring does not need שחיטה, so רב משרשיא's problem does not apply. The only open issue is the father's forbidden leg.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for a specific case; this sets up the real case being discussed
Went to, meaning mated with
Like itself, of the same type

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for where it mated with a בן פקועה like itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דַּאֲזַל אַבֶּן פְּקוּעָה דִּכְוָותֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 8 and 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about mating with a normal animal, which would be a problem for every בן פקועה
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is two בני פקועה mating, so only the father's forbidden leg is in question

steps.title: Does each limb make its matching limb, or is the seed mixed?
steps.stepSummary: The question is framed: does the father's forbidden limb only produce the matching limb in the offspring, which could be cut off, or is the father's seed mixed through the whole offspring?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Does a limb produce a matching limb, so one can cut that limb off and the rest is permitted? Or perhaps the father's seed is mixed through the whole body?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the case is clear, the גמרא spells out the question as two possible sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says only the offspring's matching leg is forbidden, so cutting it off fixes the problem. Side two says the father's seed spreads through the whole offspring, which would make the whole animal suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb produces its matching limb
Cuts off
Its seed is mixed through the whole offspring
Or perhaps; introduces the second side of a question

phrases.english: What is the law?
Does a limb produce a matching limb,
phrases.notes: This means the father's leg that came out of the womb, which stayed forbidden.

phrases.english: so one cuts it off and the rest is permitted,
or perhaps its seed is mixed throughout?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבי ירמיה's question now that the case is defined
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the forbidden limb affects only the matching limb of the offspring or the whole offspring

steps.title: Obviously the seed is mixed, or blind parents would have blind young
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה himself rejects the question: it is obvious the seed is mixed, because otherwise a blind animal would always give birth to a blind one and an amputee to an amputee.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: It is obvious that the seed is mixed. If not, a blind animal would give birth to a blind one, and an amputee would give birth to an amputee!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה takes back the question as he framed it, saying one side is obviously right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each limb produced its own matching limb, a parent missing an eye or a leg would pass that defect on, and that does not happen. So the idea that a limb produces a limb is wrong, and the question cannot stay in this form.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said; the speaker comes back and changes his view
It is obvious
Blind
An amputee, missing a limb

phrases.english: He then said:
It is obvious that its seed is mixed,
for if it were so,
a blind animal would give birth to a blind one,
and an amputee would give birth to an amputee!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first side of step 11's question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the first side of step 11's question (that a limb produces its matching limb); the second side, that the seed is mixed, is accepted as obvious and becomes the basis for step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The idea that a limb produces its matching limb is disproved because blind or amputee parents do not have blind or amputee young

steps.title: Two prohibitions are allowed, but what about a third?
steps.stepSummary: The question is reframed: every animal grows partly from its parents' forbidden חלב and דם and is still permitted. Does the same leniency cover the forbidden limb, or does it stop at two איסורים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the seed is mixed, and this is what we are asking: a normal animal comes from the strength of forbidden fat and blood, and it is still permitted. Is this case no different? Or perhaps we accept two prohibitions, but not three?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the seed is mixed, the גמרא restates רבי ירמיה's question in a new form. This is the real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal is formed partly from its parents' forbidden חלב and דם, yet it is permitted, so maybe the forbidden limb is no different. On the other hand, perhaps the Torah allowed only those two איסורים to be part of an animal's makeup, and a third איסור, the limb, makes the offspring forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From the strength or influence of
Forbidden fat
Blood, which is forbidden to eat
It is no different
Two prohibitions

steps.whatToRemember: The final question is not about biology. It asks whether the leniency for an animal formed from forbidden חלב and דם also covers a third איסור, the forbidden limb.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that its seed is mixed,
and this is what we are asking:
An ordinary animal,
doesn't it come from the strength of forbidden fat and blood,
and yet it is permitted?
Here too, it is no different.
Or perhaps:
two prohibitions we accept,
but three we do not accept?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא דְּמִבַּלְבַּל זַרְעֵיהּ, וְהָכִי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected form of the question with a new one
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the leniency for an animal formed from forbidden חלב and דם also applies to a third איסור, the forbidden limb

steps.title: Which opinion could ever have all three prohibitions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the framing of step 13. According to רבי מאיר there is no איסור יוצא, and according to רבי יהודה there is no איסור חלב ודם. So no one has three איסורים together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to whom are you asking this? If according to רבי מאיר, there is a prohibition of חלב and דם, but there is no prohibition of a limb that left. If according to רבי יהודה, there is a prohibition of a limb that left, but there is no prohibition of חלב and דם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the question from step 13 by asking which תנא could hold that one animal has all three prohibitions at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 assumed one animal could carry three איסורים: חלב, דם, and a limb that left the womb. רבי מאיר treats a full-term fetus as its own animal, so חלב and דם apply but a limb leaving the womb does not matter. רבי יהודה treats the fetus as part of its mother, so the limb that left is forbidden but its חלב is permitted. Either way you only ever get two איסורים, never three.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition on a fetus's limb that came out of the womb before the mother was slaughtered
Forbidden fats and blood
There is / there is not
And according to whom?

steps.confusionAlert: The קשיא is not saying the three איסורים are impossible in real life. It is saying no single opinion treats all three as forbidden in the same animal.

phrases.english: And according to whom?
phrases.notes: Which תנא would say one animal has all three prohibitions from step 13?

phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Meir –
there is a prohibition of forbidden fat and blood,
but there is no prohibition of a limb that left.
If according to Rabbi Yehuda –
there is a prohibition of a limb that left,
but there is no prohibition of forbidden fat and blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'two versus three איסורים' framing of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 13 that a single animal could carry חלב, דם and איסור יוצא together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each תנא accepts only one side. רבי מאיר has חלב and דם without יוצא, and רבי יהודה has יוצא without חלב and דם. So the three-איסור case never exists under one view.

steps.title: The source: גיד הנשה and חלב in a full-term fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא where רבי מאיר says גיד הנשה and חלב apply to a שליל, and רבי יהודה says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: גיד הנשה applies to a full-term fetus, and its fat is forbidden. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: it does not apply to the fetus, and its fat is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claims of step 14 by quoting the ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids the fetus's גיד הנשה and חלב, so he views it as an independent animal. That is why the יוצא rule does not apply for him. רבי יהודה permits them, so he views the fetus as part of the mother. That is why the יוצא rule applies but חלב does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, forbidden to eat
A fetus, here one that completed its term and was found inside its slaughtered mother
Applies (said of a prohibition)
Its forbidden fat

phrases.english: As we learned:
The sciatic nerve applies to the fetus,
and its fat is forbidden,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It does not apply to the fetus,
and its fat is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the two positions used in the challenge of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each hold only one side: either חלב applies or יוצא applies, never both.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about whether גיד הנשה and חלב apply to a שליל.

steps.title: Whatever grows through a forbidden thing is still permitted
steps.stepSummary: The 'two versus three' question falls away. The גמרא concludes that something produced through the strength of a forbidden thing is not forbidden because of that, so the offspring is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, anything that comes through the strength of a forbidden thing — don't we say that it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the three-איסור question cannot stand, the גמרא drops it and states the general rule: what grows through the strength of something forbidden is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 worried that a third forbidden source might be one too many. Steps 14-15 showed there is never really a third under one view. So we fall back on the basic principle that an animal is not forbidden just because forbidden things helped produce it, and the offspring of such a fetus is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the strength or influence of (here, of a forbidden thing)
That it is permitted
Rather (drops the earlier approach)

steps.whatToRemember: No one opinion has חלב, דם and איסור יוצא together in one animal. רבי מאיר has only חלב and דם, and רבי יהודה has only יוצא. The rule that what comes through the strength of a forbidden thing is permitted stays in place.

phrases.english: Rather, anything that comes through the strength of [a forbidden thing],
phrases.notes: 'A forbidden thing' isn't written, but it's understood. Here it's the parents' forbidden parts that the offspring grew from.

phrases.english: don't we say that it is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כֹּל מִכֹּחַ לָא אָמְרִינַן דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the step 13 framing, which steps 14-15 showed cannot stand, and settles on the general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Something produced through the strength of a forbidden thing is not forbidden for that reason. So the offspring of a fetus with a forbidden limb is permitted, and the question was not about such an animal.

steps.title: The real question: may one drink this animal's milk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says its true question is about drinking the milk of the animal that had a forbidden limb. Regular milk is permitted even though it comes from a live animal, but maybe that is only because שחיטה can make that animal permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we are really asking: may one drink its milk? Regular milk is like a limb from a living animal, and it is still permitted, so this milk should be no different. Or maybe there, the animal's prohibition can be fixed through שחיטה, while here the prohibition cannot be fixed through שחיטה?
steps.whatsHappening: After the 'two versus three איסורים' question fell away, the גמרא states the question it really meant to ask. The question is about drinking the milk of this animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that permits says that all milk comes from a live animal, yet the תורה allows it, so this milk should be allowed too. The side that forbids says regular milk is allowed because שחיטה can make that animal permitted. The forbidden limb here can never be made permitted by שחיטה, so its milk might stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: we are asking / it is a question for us
to drink, to gulp down
a limb taken from a living animal, which is forbidden to eat
a fix, a way to make the forbidden thing permitted
kosher slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: 'Its milk' is not the milk of a regular animal. It is the milk of the animal whose limb became forbidden, and the question is whether that forbidden status passes into its milk.

phrases.english: And this is what we are asking:
What is the law about drinking its milk?
Regular milk

phrases.aramaic: לָא כְּאֵבֶר מִן הַחַי דָּמֵי, וּשְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: isn't it like a limb from a living animal, and yet it is permitted?
So this one too should be no different.
Or perhaps there, with regular milk,
its prohibition has a fix through slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא לֵית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ בִּשְׁחִיטָה?
phrases.english: while here, its prohibition has no fix through slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected framing of step 13 with the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the milk of an animal with a forbidden limb permitted like ordinary milk, or forbidden because the limb's prohibition can never be fixed by שחיטה?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds no answer to the milk question and leaves it standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the milk question without a decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the question remain reasonable. No source decides between them, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: 'let it stand': the question is left without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: The milk of an animal with a forbidden limb is a question with no answer (תיקו). The open issue is whether milk is permitted only when it comes from an animal that שחיטה can make permitted.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 17 without resolving it.

steps.title: What is the source for permitting pieces cut from a fetus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of cutting pieces from a fetus inside its mother and asks for the source of the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who cuts from a fetus, and so on.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks where the rule comes from. This sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that pieces cut from a fetus and left inside the mother become permitted through the mother's שחיטה. One might have expected them to be forbidden as limbs cut from a living animal, so the גמרא wants a תורה source.

keyTerms.meaning: a fetus still inside its mother
from where do we know this?

phrases.english: One who cuts from a fetus, and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, the case where pieces are cut from the fetus and left inside the mother.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the mother's שחיטה permits pieces cut from the fetus.

steps.title: The source: 'an animal inside an animal'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'בהמה … בבהמה' in the פסוק as 'an animal inside an animal,' which includes the fetus in the mother's permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And every animal that has a split hoof, and so on.' The words 'animal … in the animal' come to include the offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that permits the fetus through its mother's שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק begins with 'every בהמה' and ends with 'בבהמה.' Read together, they mean 'an animal that is inside an animal,' which is the fetus. The fetus is therefore treated as part of the mother, and her שחיטה covers it, even the pieces cut from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'an animal in an animal': a fetus inside its mother
to include, to add a case
offspring, here the fetus

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And every animal that has a split hoof, and so on,'
'animal … in the animal':
phrases.notes: These are the first and last words of that same פסוק, read together as one phrase.

phrases.english: this comes to include the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'בהמה … בבהמה' includes the fetus, so the mother's שחיטה permits it.

steps.title: Challenge: then תמורה should work on a fetus
steps.stepSummary: If 'בהמה בבהמה' means a fetus, then the תמורה verse, which uses the same words, should let one make a substitute for a sanctified fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, one should be able to make a substitute for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading it just gave. It points to a problem from another area of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמורה פסוק also says 'בהמה בבהמה.' If those words mean a fetus, then a person should be able to swap an ordinary animal for the sanctified fetus of a pregnant קרבן, and the swapped animal would become holy. The גמרא assumes this is not so, so the reading of the words is now in question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'but if so': introduces a challenge built on the last claim
they may substitute (from תְּמוּרָה, swapping an animal for a sanctified one)

phrases.english: But if so,
one should be able to substitute for it!
phrases.notes: The תמורה פסוק (ויקרא 27:10) also says 'בהמה בבהמה,' so the same reading would work there too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בהמה בבהמה' as referring to a fetus.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear in the תמורה פסוק. If they mean a fetus there too, תמורה should take effect with a sanctified fetus, which is assumed not to be the law.

steps.title: The משנה in תמורה says no substitution with fetuses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a משנה: a fetus or limbs cannot be used in a substitution (תמורה) at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: you cannot substitute limbs for fetuses, fetuses for limbs, limbs and fetuses for whole animals, or whole animals for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 21 by quoting a משנה. The משנה clearly says a fetus has no part in תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said that if 'בהמה בבהמה' means a fetus, the same words in the תמורה verse should include a fetus too. But the משנה says a fetus can never be part of a substitution. So reading 'בהמה בבהמה' as a fetus must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a substitute (תמורה) for a sanctified animal
Limbs, parts of an animal
Fetuses inside the mother
Whole animals

phrases.english: Why, then, did we learn: One cannot make a substitute
neither limbs for fetuses,
nor fetuses for limbs,
nor limbs and fetuses for whole animals,
nor whole animals for them!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the limbs and fetuses. Either way, no substitution works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge of step 21 by bringing the משנה that contradicts it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בהמה בבהמה' as a fetus (step 20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words in the תמורה verse would include a fetus, but the משנה says a fetus is excluded from תמורה.

steps.title: A new source: 'and every animal' includes the fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the old reading and learns the fetus's permission from the extra word 'וכל' in 'וכל בהמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says 'And every animal' to include the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on 'בהמה בבהמה' and brings a different word from the פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכל', 'and every', is read as adding something extra: the fetus. This source belongs only to the laws of eating, so it does not cause any problem with תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier idea for a new one
To include something extra
Offspring, here the fetus

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the working source for the rest of the sugya, and the next challenges test how far it reaches.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse states:
'And every animal',
to include the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing the source that was rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fetus was included through 'בהמה בבהמה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fetus is included through the extra word 'וכל'.

steps.title: Why not also pieces cut from the spleen or kidneys?
steps.stepSummary: If 'וכל' adds things, it should also permit pieces cut from the mother's own organs. But the משנה forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even pieces cut from the spleen or kidneys should be permitted. But the משנה says pieces cut from the fetus are permitted, and pieces from the spleen or kidneys are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new source. Why does 'וכל' include only the fetus and not cut pieces of the mother herself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word could include anything. Our משנה makes a split: cut fetus pieces are permitted, cut organ pieces are forbidden. The גמרא wants to know what makes that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; testing where the new idea leads
Cuts off a piece while the animal is alive
Spleen
Kidneys

phrases.english: If so, even if one cuts
from the spleen and from the kidneys, it should also be permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה תְּנַן: חוֹתֵךְ מִן הָעוּבָּר שֶׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ –
phrases.english: why then did we learn: One who cuts from the fetus in her womb –
it is permitted to eat,
but from the spleen and from the kidneys –
it is forbidden to eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ חוֹתֵךְ מִן הַטְּחוֹל וּמִן הַכְּלָיוֹת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new 'וכל' source against our משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'וכל' includes extra things, it should also include cut organ pieces, but the משנה forbids them.

steps.title: 'It': only a whole animal, not missing pieces
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אותה' limits the permission to the whole animal, so pieces cut from the mother's body stay forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'it': whole, and not lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another word in the פסוק that sets a limit on the permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותה' means the animal as one whole unit. Pieces cut off the mother are 'missing' from her, so her שחיטה does not permit them. A piece cut from the fetus is still part of the fetus that 'וכל' includes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It'; read as 'the animal itself, as a whole'
Whole, complete
Lacking, missing a part

steps.whatToRemember: 'וכל' includes the fetus. 'אותה' excludes pieces cut from the mother. Together they explain the משנה.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'it' –
phrases.notes: From the end of the same פסוק, דברים 14:6: 'בבהמה אותה תאכלו', 'of the animal, it you may eat.'

phrases.english: whole, and not lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spleen and kidneys challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותה' limits the permission to the whole animal. Missing pieces of the mother are excluded.

steps.title: Then a dove-shaped fetus should be permitted
steps.stepSummary: If 'וכל בהמה' includes whatever is inside the animal, a dove-shaped fetus should be permitted. But רבי יוחנן forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, one who slaughters an animal and finds a dove-shaped fetus inside should be allowed to eat it. Why then does רבי יוחנן say it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'וכל' source again, this time from a ruling of רבי יוחנן. The answer is not given here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'וכל' includes the fetus just because it is inside the slaughtered animal, the shape of the fetus should not matter. רבי יוחנן forbids a fetus shaped like a dove. So the source seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so; pushing an idea to its end
The shape of a dove
It should be permitted

phrases.english: But now, if so,
one who slaughters an animal
and finds in it the shape of a dove, it should be permitted?
Why then did רבי יוחנן say:
One who slaughters an animal
and finds in it the shape of a dove,
it is forbidden to eat?
phrases.notes: Some versions say אסור and some say אֲסוּרָה. Either way, it means 'forbidden.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה וּמָצָא בָּהּ דְּמוּת יוֹנָה תִּשְׁתְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge to the 'וכל' source after the spleen and kidneys question was answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If anything inside the animal is included, a dove-shaped fetus should be permitted, but רבי יוחנן forbids it.
